messages.subject: replacing linkage map
parts:
Hello all,

I have two independent cross objects with two linkage maps.  I would like to change one cross object to have the same linkage map as the other.  They share all marker names but in some cases the two linkage maps have placed individual markers on different linkage groups.  I have tried 'replacemap' but it seems that maybe it goes linkage group by linkage group (which in these two crosses may have different numbers of markers), so it throws an error:

Error in replacemap.cross(kl.shared.renamed, pull.map(lk.shared)) :
  Number of markers don't match.

In sum, I would like to combine the genotype and phenotype data of one cross object and use the linkage map from another cross object.  The objects share the same marker names but not necessarily the same linkage group information.

Any suggestions on how to convert the map, other than a lot of cutting and pasting in a spreadsheet file?

Thanks!
Kevin

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] replacing linkage map
parts:
You can align things with a bit of R code, using movemarker()

Say x1 and x2 are the two crosses, and you want the markers in x2 to be in the same organized as they are in x1.

x2.fixed <- x2

# locations of x2 markers in cross x1
pos <- find.markerpos(x1, markernames(x2))

# for those found, move to position in x1
for(i in which(!is.na(pos[,1])) )
x2.fixed <- movemarker(x2.fixed, rownames(pos)[i], pos[i,1], pos[i,2])

# perhaps drop the markers that weren't in x1
x2.fixed <- drop.markers(x2.fixed, rownames(pos)[is.na(pos[,1])])

# probably need to sort the chromosomes
x2.fixed$geno <- x2.fixed$geno[names(x1$geno)]

The last line won't work if x1 has linkage groups whose markers are not in x2. Let me know if you need further explanation or clarification.
> "other than a lot of cutting and pasting in a spreadsheet file?"

I suspect you wrote that just to see my reaction. I've stayed remarkably calm.

karl

parts:
Karl,
Thank you for the input file.  I like your method - it is what I was looking for.  I recently was just trying to output QTLcart files where there is a separate mapfile from the cross file.  Then I was going to load the second map file with the first cross file etc..
I am glad you stayed calm with my comment.  I, of course, would not have done the spreadsheet copying and pasting!  I have been there and have learned that it should just never be done!

I will work with your elegant solution to the problem!

Thank you again,
Cheers,
Kevin
